producer_report.summary: Added intervention category `mistake` (closed list now 9) and `Intervention::is_mistake()`: category `mistake`, or `other` with text starting `Mistake:`. That prefix rule counts the eleven back-filled records without rewriting them. `athena status` (text and JSON `mistakes`, separate from the raw `interventions_by_category`) and `athena audit` report the total, counts per class of work, and per cause. A cause is the failure-class name of the mistake's newest recorded introspection, or "not yet introspected". Each cause entry has a recurring mark and the prevention kind, prevention and proposed request from its newest introspection, so repeat causes collapse into one entry with one proposal. Introspecting a mistake maps it to category `mistake` (including the prefix records) and adds an instruction to the prompt to name the check or knowledge that would have prevented it and to pick the recurring cause as the failure class. Root cause addressed: back-filled mistakes were stored as `other` and nothing could find them. Tests added; fmt, clippy and the full test run pass.

checks_run.note: First run flagged one sort_by; fixed with sort_by_key.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: new tests pass. They show that an intervention logged with category `mistake` is accepted by the parser and `InterventionCategory::ALL`, and that an unknown category is still rejected with the list including `mistake`.
criteria_check.evidence: records.rs test `mistake_is_a_category_and_unknown_ones_stay_unknown` (ALL length 9, parse). lifecycle.rs test `the_mistake_category_is_accepted_and_an_unknown_one_is_refused_with_the_list`: intervene with `mistake` succeeds; `bogus` fails with an error naming both bogus and mistake. All pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test with several mistake interventions of different classes and causes shows that status and the audit output report mistake counts per class and per cause, and that the JSON has those breakdowns separate from `interventions_by_category`.
criteria_check.evidence: introspection.rs `mistakes_are_counted_per_class_and_cause_and_repeat_causes_share_one_proposal`: three mistakes across docs and code and two causes. It asserts status JSON `mistakes.total`, `by_class`, `by_cause`, the separate `interventions_by_category` (mistake 2, other 1), and the rendered status text. `athena audit` prints the same MistakeReport through `Athena::mistakes()` and `display::mistakes`. The audit command itself is not run in a test, because it needs a scripted auditor model.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test`: a test shows that introspecting a `mistake` intervention produces a proposal naming the check or knowledge that would have prevented it. Repeat causes aggregate into one proposal.
criteria_check.evidence: Same test: the prompt carries the instruction with category `mistake`, the stored introspection has a non-empty prevention, and two mistakes sharing a failure class give one by_cause entry with count 2, recurring, and one prevention (the newest). The status text shows `prevent [code-check] ...` and `propose ...`.

criteria_check.criterion: Existing records with category `other` and text starting 'Mistake:' (the eleven back-filled on 2026-10-23) are counted as mistakes in status and the audit. Records are not rewritten. The text-prefix rule is documented in a code comment or doc.
criteria_check.evidence: The same introspection.rs test logs an `other` intervention with 'Mistake:' text, which is counted (total 3) and introspected as category `mistake`. The record file bytes are unchanged after status runs. The prefix rule is in the doc comment on `Intervention::is_mistake`, and in the README and the changelog.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check` both exited 0.

criteria_check.criterion: Outcome-check: a reader of the status or audit output can see how many mistakes occurred, which classes and causes recur, and which prevention work was proposed. Output is not only a type or field addition.
criteria_check.evidence: The rendered text is asserted in the tests: `mistakes    3 · by class: code 1, docs 2`, `×2 (recurring)`, `prevent [code-check] ...`, `propose ...`, and `no prevention proposed yet: not introspected` for a mistake without an introspection.

open_issues: Departure from plan: I edited docs/design/athena-v0.md (category table) because it lists the closed categories; it was not on the deliverables list.
Departure from plan: manage.rs and reading.rs needed no edits, because the unknown-category message is built from ALL and no match was exhaustive.
Departure from plan: no blank-prevention flag in introspect.rs, because `IntrospectionRecord::validate` already requires every field on a recorded introspection.
Departure from plan: the `next` command for un-introspected causes was dropped, because no introspect command exists. The text lists the intervention ids instead.
The `athena audit` CLI path is not covered end to end by a test, because it needs a scripted auditor. Only the shared report builder and its renderer, through status, are tested.
Mistakes with no job and no introspection are never fed into defaults proposals (proposals.rs untouched, as planned).
mistakes: I left a stray comment in a test and removed it. I edited docs/design/athena-v0.md, which was not on the deliverables list, because the category list there would otherwise be out of date.
learnings: `athena audit <job>` is a model-run per-job outcome audit, not a repository-wide report. I added the mistakes block to its text and JSON output as the plan said.
There is no `athena introspect` command. Interventions are introspected only at `intervene` time or on correction, so back-filled records may have no introspection and show as 'not yet introspected'.
FailureClass names live in `Records.classes`, and an introspection's `failure_class` is a RecordId into them.
Bash cannot use tail or read tool-result files outside the working directory; `cargo test -q` keeps the output short.
desires: A command to introspect an existing intervention, so back-filled mistakes can get a cause and a prevention.
